ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a 4×4 small-square pattern, with black small squares respectively in row 1 column 3, row 1 column 4, row 2 column 3, row 3 column 1, and row 4 column 4, and all the other squares are white. Then reason: the problem requires making the figure have at least one axis of symmetry only by continuing to blacken some white squares. Check the possible axes of symmetry one by one: if it is symmetric about the vertical center line, many mirror-image squares need to be added; if it is symmetric about the horizontal center line, 3 squares need to be added; if it is symmetric about the main diagonal from upper left to lower right, among the existing black squares, (1,3) and (3,1) are already mirror images of each other, and (4,4) is on the diagonal and does not need to be added, only these 2 squares (4,1) and (3,2) are missing, so as long as these 2 squares are blackened again, a symmetric figure can be obtained; if it is symmetric about the other diagonal, 3 squares need to be added. After comparison, at least 2 small squares need to be blackened.

raw_record.question_text: What is the smallest number of little squares that need to be painted to get at least one axis of symmetry in the picture?

method.method_draft: Model the picture as a 4 by 4 grid with black squares at row-column positions (1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (3,1), and (4,4). Since only additional little squares may be painted, test each possible symmetry axis of the square grid by counting how many mirror partners of existing black squares are still white. For the vertical axis, 5 partners are missing; for the horizontal axis, 3 are missing; for the main diagonal from top-left to bottom-right, only (4,1) and (3,2) must be painted; for the other diagonal, 3 are missing. The smallest count is therefore 2, achieved by making the picture symmetric about the main diagonal.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is a direct exhaustive symmetry-axis check: it converts the image into grid coordinates, evaluates every possible axis, and chooses the minimum number of forced added squares.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the 4x4 grid and identify the currently painted black cells: top row columns 3 and 4, second row column 3, third row column 1, and fourth row column 4.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question’s requirement that the answer is the smallest number of little squares to paint so that the final picture has at least one axis of symmetry.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply the rule that a figure is symmetric about an axis if every painted square has a painted mirror-image square across that axis; because painting only adds black squares, each missing mirror partner must be counted as a required new painted square.
